liveRoast.title: Title *
liveRoast.noSerialPortsDetected: No serial ports detected -- plug your adapter in, then ↻.
liveRoast.separateDrivePortPlaceholder: only if your own wiring needs a 2nd connection for Air/Drum
liveRoast.usingProfileHint: Using the "{{name}}" register map -- the advanced fields below don't apply while a profile is selected. Pick "Custom" above to go back to setting individual registers by hand.
liveRoast.advancedModbusHint: Leave any of these blank to use the FZ-94 defaults above. Only worth touching once you've confirmed your own unit's actual register map differs (see the VFD's own nameplate/front-panel parameters, or a real probe's slave ID). BT/ET/DT/Burner are confirmed against a shipped FZ-94 machine preset and its interpreting source code — exposed here for a genuinely different Modbus roaster, not because a real FZ-94 should need them changed. Air/Drum (control+feedback registers, operating range) and the Burner SV°C range are that engine's least-confirmed, blog-sourced defaults.
liveRoast.burnerSvPairHint: Air/Drum min+max and the Burner SV min+max only take effect as pairs — set both sides or neither.
liveRoast.ms6514Hint: Direct USB read of the Mastech MS6514 — reads straight over USB, no other software needed. Read-only. T1 → BT, T2 → ET. Keep the meter's display set to "T1" or "T2" (not "T1-T2") for reliable dual-channel reading. Every milestone (Charge, Dry End, FC Start, Drop, etc.) is a manual click — mark them yourself as the roast happens.
liveRoast.aillioHint: Talks directly to the roaster over USB (no port/host to configure — the app finds it by its own USB vendor/product id). Heater/Fan/Drum read back the device's own last-reported state, same "don't clobber real state" behavior as Direct Modbus.
liveRoast.tc4Hint: Direct USB read/write of a TC4+ shield running the aArtisanQ (PID) firmware, 115200 baud — talks straight over USB, no other software needed. Channel 1 → BT, channel 2 → ET, channel 3 (if wired) → DT. Heater and Fan sliders send real OT1/DCFAN commands; there's no Drum output on TC4, so that slider doesn't do anything here.
liveRoast.autoDetectMilestones: Auto-detect Charge/Dry End/FC Start from BT (opt-in)
liveRoast.dryEndThreshold: Dry End BT threshold (°C, blank to disable)
liveRoast.fcStartThreshold: FC Start BT threshold (°C, blank to disable)
liveRoast.startingControlsHintAlways: Sent as the roast's first command right after START, and used as the Controls panel's starting position.
liveRoast.startingControlsHintPresetOnly: Only applied at START when loaded from a saved preset (see "Load saved config" above) -- a fresh start like this one leaves the roaster wherever it already is, so it's not clobbered by an unrelated stale value. Otherwise these are just what gets saved into a new preset below.
liveRoast.milestonesHintPreset: Burner/Air/Drum start from this preset's saved values (see the Device tab), sent right after START -- from then on, the Controls panel on the Live Roast page reads and shows whatever the roaster is actually doing.
liveRoast.milestonesHintNoPreset: Burner/Air/Drum aren't set here -- once connected, the Controls panel on the Live Roast page reads and shows whatever the roaster is actually doing (from the device itself, not a guess), and nothing is written to it until you move a slider yourself.
liveRoast.pressOnHint: Press ON above when you're ready to connect.
liveRoast.mastechHint: Reading {{port}} directly — no other software needed. Read-only, this meter has no command to control anything. Every milestone (Charge, Dry End, FC Start, Drop, etc.) is a manual click — mark them yourself below.
liveRoast.resizeChartHandle: Drag to resize the chart row (controls/chart/Small Readout follow it)
liveRoast.modbusLiveHint: The controls beside the chart read and write directly over {{target}}: Burner is a drum-temperature setpoint (register 5, default 100–250°C — not a power %, shown as both a % slider and a direct °C slider that move each other), Air and Drum are VFD drives (run/stop + frequency registers 8192/8193, default 0–100%/0–70%), each with its own feedback register (8451) reporting the drive's actual current speed. Out-of-range values are clamped to the configured range. See "Advanced Modbus register map" above to override any of these for your own unit. Every milestone (Charge, Dry End, FC Start, Drop, etc.) is a manual click — mark them yourself as the roast happens.
liveRoast.tc4LiveHint: Reading/writing {{port}} directly (115200 baud, aArtisanQ/PID firmware) — no other software needed. The Heater/Fan sliders beside the chart send real OT1/DCFAN commands; there's no Drum output on TC4, so that slider doesn't do anything here. Heater/Fan readouts stay blank — TC4's own READ command only reports temperature channels, not its current output duty. Every milestone (Charge, Dry End, FC Start, Drop, etc.) is a manual click — mark them yourself as the roast happens.
